result:
Review complete. Verdict: **reject** (tier1). `review-verdict.json` written to the workspace root.

Key finding: the guard's entire enforcement rests on checking whether `INVOCATION_ID` is unset — a plain env var any interactive session (including the AI session it's meant to constrain) can spoof with `export INVOCATION_ID=x` to fully bypass the block. The shipped test even exercises this exact bypass path (labeled "systemd-simulated") without recognizing it as a forgeable escape hatch. There are also unaddressed bypasses via `command git`/full binary path/`unset -f`, `gh api .../pulls/N/merge` evading the `pr merge`-specific match, and `git push --all` from a non-protected branch still reaching master/main. None of this is disclosed in the snippet's own "known_limitation" section, which only covers the Owner-vs-AI ambiguity — so the deliverable oversells itself as real technical enforcement when it's closer to the paper rule it was meant to replace. Recommend sending back for rework rather than merging.
